outcome.answer: Ziqing Qiao and coauthors’ “Rethinking the Role of Efficient Attention in Hybrid Architectures” analyzes how efficient-attention modules affect hybrid language models [1]. It finds that full attention mainly carries long-range retrieval, while efficient attention shapes how retrieval capability develops during training; larger sliding-window windows can delay the formation of retrieval heads [1]. The authors also report that applying NoPE only to full-attention layers in a small-window hybrid improves long-context performance with negligible short-context impact [1].
